The test image shows soybean stems/petioles with dark brown to purplish-brown elongated discoloration running along the stems, with green pods visible. Key features: stem disease, dark streaking lesions, purplish-brown color.

Top candidates: Anthracnose, Diaporthe, Phomopsis, Brown_Stem_Rot. Let me compare reference images.
The Anthracnose reference (bottom-right panel) shows green pods with dark brown elongated stem/petiole lesions very similar to the test image. Let me check a few more candidates to confirm.

None of these match as well. Charcoal Rot shows silvery/dead stems; Rhizoctonia is soil-line seedling disease; Phytophthora shows wilting; SDS shows interveinal chlorosis on leaves. Let me check a few more to be thorough.

Septoria Brown Spot = leaf spots only; Fusarium = root/crown rot; Cercospora = leaf spots; Bacterial Blight = leaf lesions. None match.

**Summary of analysis:**
- **Test image**: Close-up of soybean stem/petiole with dark brown to purplish-brown elongated discoloration running along the stems, with green pods visible — clearly a stem disease at pod-fill stage
- **Best match**: **Anthracnose** — the Anthracnose reference (bottom-right panel) shows exactly this: dark brown elongated lesions on petioles/stems with green pods present. Anthracnose (Colletotrichum truncatum) is known to cause dark brown to purplish-black lesions running along stems and petioles at mid-to-late season
- **Ruled out**: Diaporthe/Phomopsis (pod/seed lesions with pycnidia), Brown Stem Rot (internal browning + interveinal chlorosis), Charcoal Rot (silvery-gray dead stems), Rhizoctonia (seedling soil-line lesions), all leaf-spot diseases
